items.title: Derived completion has finite cohomological dimension bounded by the number of generators of the ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The statement is that derived completion with respect to an ideal generated by r elements has finite cohomological dimension, in the form of two statements comparing the completions along a morphism whose cohomology is an isomorphism in a range: one for the range at least one, and one for the range at most minus one with a shift of r (statement lines 26507-26522). The proof writes the completion as a derived limit of Koszul complexes, obtains the short exact sequence computing its cohomology, and then analyses the cone of the given morphism in the two cases: in the first case the cone vanishes in nonnegative degrees and the Koszul complexes sit in nonpositive degrees, while in the second the Koszul complexes sit between minus r and zero, which produces the shift visible in the statement (proof lines 26524-26552). The degree bookkeeping around the displayed sequence is what makes both assertions follow from the same computation. The counted span refers twice to earlier results of this chapter, carried as navigation stubs.
